main_independent_findings: setPlacedBy appends a Player profile directly before super; actual membership production is shown, but the superclass placement body and outer registry/runtime are not newly certified.

The first sharedUsers element defines owner; add uses UUID-else-name dedup while removal by name can remove the first element. Local MainMenu/whitelist/owner guards do not certify the outer C2S dispatcher; redstone parsing precedes them.
SharedUsers and HackedUsers name/UUID encodings are reached by parent save/load virtual calls through the ticking class. This is storage coding, but mutation dirtiness and actual flush are unproved.
The reader clears then parses shared before hacked; malformed UUID can leave partially replaced state and no catch/transaction is shown. Null UUID writing is not protected here.

Positive rebootTimer bypass, shared profile membership and old hacked membership are current authorization inputs. Station tick138–171 was not read anew; no expiry, revoke-time or lifetime claim is made.
Player contains(profile) and UUID overload comparison differ; GameProfile equals implementation and offline identity semantics remain dependencies.
clearRemoved/setRemoved add/remove after super; cache side partition, weak membership and world identity unload removal support current lookup, without proving chunk reload reconstruction.
Actual lookup filters removed/dimension/network and inclusive spatial bounds; placement of another station uses inflated16. Range-manager internals and coverage persistence are not read.
Any denying eligible station protects the location; another allowing station does not override it. Counts, UUID overloads, graph slots and axis variants are support within this single policy.
The complete network graph checks require one subroutine/IO/registry and connecting paths; they support active eligibility rather than extra independent credit.
HIGHEST interaction handler requires ServerPlayer and loaded target; right-click station itself is exempt while left-click is not. Local interaction does not call the place/break exemption helper.
Interaction denial explicitly requests RED overlay feedback and, for BlockItem, a selected-slot packet before returning false for event cancellation. It does not infer denial from absent damage.

The interaction stack may be offhand while packet index still uses inventory.selected. This is a source-level argument mismatch risk, not a proven client corruption or exploitable runtime bug; packet consumer is unreviewed.

Multiplace cancels the passed event at first protected snapshot; single place and break cancel their own events with RED messages. Engine rollback and subsequent event-bus arbitration remain unproved.
Creative/config or permission2 exemptions appear in place/break/explosion, not local interaction; entry-point differences are observations, not a confirmed bypass.

ExplosionStart only removes protected positions for indirect Player/server/nonexempt source; list-population/rebuild timing is unreviewed. This is not confirmed anti-explosion protection or total event cancellation.

Station useWithoutItem gates network/already-hacked/security level then may invoke old hacking; shift PASS and unconditional terminal SUCCESS do not certify menu access. Failure hurt result is ignored.

Old simulation edge/cancel/retaliation/addHacker, old projectile-owner suppression, permanent retame, foreign-owner damage denial, hostility reversal and saved migration inventory readers remain their complete old owners.

This one policy concerns persisted area membership plus eligible multistation any-denier and action-specific explicit refusal/correction requests; it is not a new hack-grant, generic NBT migration, entity damage immunity or late-event arbitration.
The fixed source uses NeoForge/new APIs; no 1.20.1 port, deployed registration, native Boss feedback, client visual, temporal completeness or production compatibility has been validated.
